title: Canonical models for two intermediate propositional logics

based_on.title: Intuitionistic Logic, Winter 2019/20 (notes dated January 2, 2020)
based_on.pages: §2, printed pp.26–29: Definitions30–39, Lemmas8–9, Theorems13–14; the full KC directed-canonical argument. LC comparability is developed locally from the same prime-theory construction.

summary: Construct fixed canonical models proving strong completeness and compactness for weak excluded middle and Dummett’s principle.
abstract: Weak excluded middle is valid when any two possible futures can join, while Dummett’s principle is valid when they can be compared. Do these frame conditions account for every consequence of adding the corresponding principles to intuitionistic logic? We prove that they do, even for infinitely many premises in the language with numbered atoms. We keep the earlier canonical worlds that contain all instances of the chosen principle, and show that their order has the required directed or linear future cones. One fixed model for each axiom set then supplies a counterexample to every failed deduction. This gives strong completeness, compactness and rooted countermodels, while leaving the separate question of finite countermodels open.
